opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Santos (employee ID E050) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E050.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Santos (E050) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write (admin only if their role owns the system; the Engineer role owns Source Code, but write was requested). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E050 is a contractor with basic security training (note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing full_time). Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training caps access at read; requested write exceeds that. Recommend granting read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: one lists full_time, the other (from the Security database) lists contractor with basic security training. The Security note explicitly flags this conflict. Under policy, contractors with basic training are capped at read, and write (the requested level) exceeds that maximum, so the maximum of read should be granted. Given the conflicting evidence, the more restrictive, policy-compliant level is read.
